target_customer: Real estate investors who buy single family homes and want higher rent, plus renters who want a cheap room
problem: Affordable housing is scarce in young person cities, and investors earn less renting a whole house than renting by the room.
business_model: Master lease with guaranteed rent to the investor; HomeRoom keeps about 15 percent of collections (per Dealroom)
product_category: Co-living and rent by the room property management

founders.name: Johnny Wolff
founders.background_notes: Financial analyst in Silicon Valley, then full time real estate investor in Austin.

founders.name: Thomas Hornbeck
education: Computer science PhD, left in fifth year (ABD)

founders.name: Mike Tich
founders.background_notes: Marketing science, product and data science roles.

competitors.name: Bungalow
competitors.what: Master leases whole homes and rents individual bedrooms
competitors.traction_then: Described as fastest growing shared living startup in 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly operations: sourcing, renovation, tenant vetting and rent collection, with modest software and ML claims.

defensibility.rationale: Bungalow and PadSplit ran similar models, and execution depended on local operations rather than proprietary technology.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bungalow acquired HomeRoom per Dealroom and Seedtable, date disputed.

market_need_then: The company reported 105 homes in 31 cities, 1.8M USD rental GMV in 2021 (300 percent YoY) and rents about 50 percent below market comps; all self reported on its YC page.

branding.domain_note: Used livehomeroom.com; the YC listing carried no website.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain pitch: rent your property by the room and earn 50 percent more.

branding.brand_signature: RentByTheRoom as a product line launched via newswire.
branding.community_and_virality: A BigPockets forum thread and review blogs discussed the service, mixed in tone; one competitor blog published a review.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a common word shared with many education and software brands, and brand coverage was limited to forums and reviews.

outcome_analysis: HomeRoom grew a rent by the room model from one Kansas City home in 2018 to 105 homes by 2021, raised a 1M USD pre-seed around YC W22 and a further seed in March 2022, then was acquired by Bungalow. The deal price and exact date are not public, so it is unclear whether it was a strong exit or a soft landing.
notes: Acquisition date conflicts: Dealroom says 2025, Seedtable lists 1 Jan 2024; Bungalow has a transition page for HomeRoom customers; price undisclosed. A March 2022 seed (YC, 1984 Ventures, First Check, BBQ Capital per Parsers VC via Seedtable) has no verified amount and is not recorded. Total raised figures conflict (1.2M, 1.7M, 1.9M, 2M, and about 5M from a podcast summary). Sources disagree on headquarters (San Francisco, San Jose, Kansas). PadSplit (rooms in single family homes, launched 2017 per a partner blog) was a likely competitor but has no dated source, so it is omitted. Founder Thomas is described on the YC page as having a PhD in ML but his bio says ABD.
